bull_bear.body: Debt reduction priority (reduced debt by INR 140 Cr to ~INR 100 Cr); Dividend increased to INR 5/share (from INR 4); Organic growth funding via internal accruals; No M&A announced, focus on organic order book expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical instability in Gulf region affecting operations/visas; Sovereign spending shifts due to oil price volatility; Currency and raw material price fluctuations; Intense competition in water sector; Execution delays on mega-projects.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' over sheer top-line expansion; Strategic selectivity in bidding (sovereign/MDB funded only); Pride in technology leadership and ESG credentials; Optimistic on GCC and India long-term themes.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Entry into Kuwait and UAE markets after long gestation; Specific focus on water needs for AI data centers and semiconductor fabs as a distinct new vertical; 'Looped water grid' in Chennai as a replicable model for other Indian cities; Industrial clients reorienting business models based on reliability of Wabag's treated water supply.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash positive for the 7th year running and the 14th consecutive quarter, at INR 9,649 Mn excluding HAM (INR 8,566 Mn including HAM projects); management describes this as reflecting "the quality of order book and cash management".
- Asset-light business model is the stated capital philosophy, with RoCE of 19.6% (outlook >20%) and RoE of 16% (outlook >15%) described as "Creating long term Shareholder Value".
- Medium-term outlook (3-5 years): order book >4x of revenue (currently 3x of revenue at ~INR 194 Bn), revenues 15-20% CAGR, EBITDA margin 13-15%, O&M at 20% of total revenues, and net cash positive.
- Credit rating of AA-/Stable and A1+; employees given shared ownership through ESOPs.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Municipal (80% of rev) vs Industrial (20%); EPC (83%) vs O&M (17% - targeting 20%); India vs ROW split approx 50:50 in order inflow; O&M backlog provides annuity-like cash flows with 10-20 year contract tenors.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Among the World's Top 3* Largest Private Water Operator and Desalination Plant Suppliers" (*As per GWI Survey 2024), with 25+ countries presence and 96+ Mn lives touched globally.
- Century-old lineage: WABAG Wasserfilterbau founded in Wroclaw in 1924, VA TECH WABAG Ltd. Chennai founded in 1996, management buyout backed by ICICI Venture in 2005, reunification with WABAG Austria Group in 2007, IPO in 2010; the deck frames 2024 onward as "Century 2.0: Pioneering the Next 100 Years".
- Moat framed around technology and IP: 125+ IPRs developed in-house, global R&D centres in Europe and India, and "Core Expertise in Engineering & Procurement (EP)".
- Management states the wins "reflect our focus on complex technology jobs which fall in our focus area", achieved "even as we persisted with our selective approach to bidding for projects".
- Asset Light Model with AA-/Stable and A1+ credit rating.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Governance] All seven Board committees are chaired by Independent Directors, and the Board has "only 2 Executive Directors out of 6 Directors"; professional management with an average 30 years of relevant experience.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 19.08%, Institutions (Domestic) 6.33%, Institutions (Foreign) 16.60%, Strategic Investor 8.02%, Non-Institutionals 48.31%; 6,23,54,776 equity shares outstanding, face value INR 2.
- [Market data] Closing market price INR 2,009 as on 30th June 2026, 52-week H/L INR 1,033 / 2,189, market capitalisation INR 12,538 Crores / USD 1,328 Mn.
- [Digitalization] Koyambedu TTRO plant runs on an AI operational-intelligence platform, an AI/ML-based NRW reduction solution is being piloted at GNN TTRO, and an AI-based Operations & Decision Support System was piloted at the AMAS plant in Bahrain, with wider digitalization of plants and networks in India and the Middle East being explored.
- [Awards] "Asia Business Leader of the Year 2026 - Company of the Year" and Most Preferred Workplace 2026-27 for the fourth consecutive year.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin sustained at 13.3% despite raw material volatility; O&M margins currently ~17% with path to 20%; Cost mitigation via value engineering and technology differentiation; Geographical diversification helps buffer currency risks.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 15-20% CAGR; Margin: EBITDA 13-15%, O&M margin target 20% (medium-term); Order Inflow: Targeting >INR 7,500 Cr annually with focus on sovereign/MDB funded mega-projects; Capex/Commissioning: Asset-light model; major commissioning expected for Asia's largest desalination plant next year.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR 17,200 Cr total; Geographic split: India 60%, ROW 40%; Segment split: O&M ~40% (INR 6,500 Cr), EPC ~60%; Key projects: Chennai 45 MLD TTRO (Rehab+O&M), Chennai City-wide Looped Water Grid, Yanbu Desalination (Saudi); Visibility: 4x revenue coverage.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New verticals: Ultra-pure water for Semiconductors, PV Cell manufacturing, Data Centers, Green Hydrogen/Ammonia; Geographic expansion: Kuwait and UAE entry imminent, Sub-Saharan Africa growth, Saudi industrial sector (Aramco) penetration; O&M scale-up to 20% of revenue mix.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: VA Tech Wabag delivered record PAT of INR 371 Cr (+26% YoY) and 20% revenue growth, driven by a robust order intake of INR 7,500 Cr including three mega-projects (>INR 1,000 Cr each). The company reinforced its 'profitable growth' mantra with a net cash position of INR 950 Cr and an order book of INR 17,200 Cr (4x revenue), signaling strong visibility despite geopolitical headwinds in the Gulf.

WABAG plans to develop 100 Bio-CNG plants globally under its partnership with Peak Sustainability Ventures, having commissioned the first project at the 70 MLD Dundaheda STP, Ghaziabad.
The Dundaheda Bio-CNG project (BOT model, via SPV Ghaziabad Bioenergy Private Limited) is expected to reduce approximately 250,000 metric tons of carbon emissions over its lifecycle.
Company remains focused on investing in high-growth emerging economies while scaling down its exposure to the European region, to maximise capital returns.

risks.note: The water infrastructure sector has long project gestation periods, leading to elongated contract award cycles; the company relies on its diversified presence across 25+ countries and multiple segments to counter this.

Operating in a cyclical, competitive infrastructure sector, profitability is sensitive to raw material price and forex movements; the company relies on natural hedges from its international presence, forex hedging and contract management.
risks.risk: Cyclical sector and foreign exchange exposure

risks.note: Strong competition from global and domestic players may pressure margins and market share; the company seeks to differentiate on technology/innovation (125+ proprietary IPRs) rather than price.

Fluctuations in input costs (steel, speciality chemicals, membranes) and supply chain disruptions can impact margins, particularly under fixed-price EPC contracts; mitigated via strategic sourcing, long-term supplier partnerships and contract price-escalation provisions.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and supply-chain disruption

risks.note: Increasingly stringent discharge norms, zero-liquid-discharge requirements and micro-pollutant standards may raise compliance costs and technical complexity; non-compliance could result in financial penalties and reputational risk.

Significant reliance on the municipal segment exposes the company to public-sector risks including procurement delays, extended payment timelines and policy/budgetary shifts, partly mitigated by multilateral-funded, federal-government and sovereign-guaranteed contracts.
risks.risk: High dependence on the municipal segment

risks.note: Key financial risks include interest rate volatility and foreign exchange fluctuations, particularly given the company's Indian Rupee-denominated operations set against a global project footprint.
risks.risk: Interest rate and foreign exchange volatility
